While First Solar’s Vietnamese and Malaysian CdTe module manufacturing facilities remain active, U.S. CdTe module imports from those countries fell in 2024 by 15%. CdTe module imports from India increased in 2024, but some of this increase may have been due to mislabeled trade data. First Solar began shifting to its larger-format, more efficient, and frameless Series 7 modules in 2023. In 2024, more than half the modules produced in the United States were Series 7, but the less efficient Series 6 model (which, unlike Series 7, has a bifacial option) constituted 62% of global production. This percentage of Series 6 modules is expected to decrease in 2025 as documented Series 7 facility announcements come online. At the end of 2024, First Solar reported average module efficiencies of 18.2% for Series 6 modules and 18.9% for Series 7, down 1.7% and 0.4% year over year, respectively, and 2.5 percentage points lower than the average efficiency of c-Si modules installed in the U.S. in 2024 (First Solar 2025a). The company did not explain the lower efficiency, but it could relate to the scale-up of manufacturing lines in 2024 or manufacturing issues reported in Q3 2024. In general, balance-of-module components are imported for Series 6 modules, from trade partners such as Malaysia, while components for Series 7 modules produced in the United States come from domestic suppliers. There is enough domestic production of cadmium for 6 GW of dc modules, but no tellurium or selenium refining exists in the United States. First Solar partners with 5N Plus in Canada to refine U.S. tellurium and produce CdTe powder. Some of the tellurium-containing residues 5N Plus refines come from Utah. However, Canada primarily imports tellurium from China, the world’s leading producer, which recently placed export control on tellurium and CdTe compounds. Most of 5N Plus CdTe powder to First Solar ships from Canada, but it may come from manufacturing facilities in Germany as well. 3.2 Global Context Figure 36a displays CdTe PV production and market share over time, showing global share decreasing from 5% to 2% during 2015–2024 even as production increased.
